answer: Throttle admission itself: every agent must solve a memory-hard puzzle whose footprint is as unique as a quartz vein before joining an activity. Raising thousands of clones forces thousands of parallel memory buys, while one honest agent solves a single proof, re-verifiable in microseconds. The cost curve, not good intentions, is the wall; a botnet founders like a dune shifting under weight, whereas a real operator barely notices the toll, and a mirror-image of an old answer never passes.
